sections.text: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ताच त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।
The knowledge, the act and the doer differ according to the Qualities. Listen to this too:
That knowledge which sees the One Indestructible in all beings, the One Indivisible in all separate lives, may be truly called Pure Knowledge.
The knowledge which thinks of the manifold existence in all beings as separate - that comes from Passion.

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. As we have discussed before, the whole exercise in Bhagavad Gita is to renounce actions in knowledge. We have figured out that actions are the cause for all my frictions and unhappiness in life. Any action which I perform, whether good, bad or ugly, will have its result. And the result will be either conducive, not conducive, or somewhere in between -- mixed. And in this chapter, Bhagavan clarifies that this only applies to those who have not given up expectation for the fruits of actions.
In this chapter we learn the definition of a Tyagi: one who gives up Karma Phala Tyaga is a Tyagi. The one who gives up all the desire-prompted actions is a Sannyasi. I can only give up all my desire-prompted actions if I have no desires. At this point, it does not seem that I can reach that point where I hold no desire. So then the question is: how can I solve this conundrum?
On one hand it says the only way you can be free is if you have no desires. On the other hand, it clearly seems that living without desires is not possible. It seems like there is something we are missing in this equation. If both are true, then there has to be some kind of parallax which I have to remove so I can see the truth as it is. This is something which we have learnt in Vedanta: that the same thing can be seen in two different lights.
A rope can be seen as a rope if Im clear about what it is. But it can also give rise to fear that its a snake. So the same thing, depending on my mental association, can appear as a rope or as a snake. Similarly, because I cant reconcile these two -- on one hand Gita keeps telling me to live without any desires and on the other hand I see that desires are unavoidable -- it seems like there are two different kinds of people: one who cannot live without desires and one who has no desires.
So to understand that, we have obviously taken this study of Bhagavad Gita. And now we are coming to the conclusion that there are two I. The one I is a conditioned I which is conditioned by my body, my mind, my intellect, associated with my body, my mind, intellect and therefore that I has all the limitations of my body, my mind and intellect. But then there is one I which is always there. No matter what the condition of this body, mind, intellect -- the body was a baby, then it was a child, then a young man, then an adult, and now its the old man -- that I remained the same. So there must be a differentiation between the I which I consider I when I think about my body, my mind, my intellect and that which has no conditioning.
When I remove all the conditioning, I will not be there as this conditioned I, but that I will still remain. As we learnt in Bhagavad Gita chapter 2, that I is indestructible. The metaphor we use all the time is the room space. Room space is conditioned by its limitations of the size and shape and the type of air in it. Right now once this walls, floor and ceilings are gone the space will remain what it is. So we have learnt in chapter 13 that there is a field and its knower. As long as there is field, I as the knower will limit myself as the knower of the field. So in this chapter we have started our journey by saying let me define what is Tyagi and what is Sannyasi.
The Tyagi does not give up the Karmaphalas, because Karmaphalas are not in his hand. Karma Phala Datta -- someone other than me -- gives me the fruits of my actions. But I want to influence that outcome by my desires. That I want this particular outcome.
That if I give up influencing the outcome by my desires then I will be Karma Falathyagi. If you know this, then the next thing you need to know is that any kind of results which come from your actions are not binding to you. Because you did not expect any result out of it. Whatever comes you accept with the Prasad Buddhi. Just like when you go to the temple and you accept Prasad, you dont really are choosy about what comes in your prasad. Whatever Panditja gives you, accept it with love.
When whatever comes out of my actions is the result, I should accept that. Just as I accept Prasad from Bhagavan. If I develop this sense, Bhagavan said, you will be a Tyagi. Once you disassociate from this limited I, you will not have desires. That higher I will not have desires. The smaller I will have desires. The body will have its own demands, mind will have its own demands and intellect will own demands.
The one who is overseeing the three will have no demands whatsoever. It is now up to me to identify either with the lower I or the higher I. So we have learned from the beginning that giving up actions is not possible. Therefore, whatever action you perform should be ordained action. Those even when I am performing, I should be not attached. It should be performed without any Ra, without any asakti, without any expectation and any attachment.
I should be performing this action without attachment. Thats the advice weve heard so far. Then Bhagavan got into the discussion of what action is, because we need to understand it. We understood that action has five components. Unless those five come together, action never takes place.
In these five components, one is Karta, the actor. You have to have an actor or an action to come into being. And thats the only one I have control over. Then I need to now define who the Karta is. And that once I figure out, then I will be able to figure out whether I am the sufferer, the enjoyer of my actions or not. Because the Karta is the Bhokta of all the actions.
So in the following _Verses_ we have seen that one who considers that this self is the doer, he does not see the truth alone. Because the truth is the self is not acting at all. In all these actions which I am performing, the self remains as just a witness. Because actions are performed by the gunas of my body, mind and intellect. The nature of my mind, nature of my intellect and nature of my body decide what type of actions Ill perform. When the conducive objects come in my way, I get tempted to act and then I act.
Gnanam, gneam, parignata, Trivedaha, Karma, Chodana. These are the propellers of my actions. Gnanam, knowledge, Gnayam the knowable and Pariganatha the knower. So this is basically going back to chapter 13. In chapter 13 we are seeing there is a field and its knower. So when this gnanam, when there is a knowledge of the field occurs, thats the knowledge.
Once I figure out this is the field of my activity and I identify it, then the knower comes into being. As long as Im aware of the field, I become the knower of the field. So this three when the knower of the field identifies the field and when that knowledge takes place the gnanam that becomes the propeller of my action. Starbucks is the field of my knowledge. Passing by I identify Starbucks.
The field of knowledge is there and my knowledge has taken place -- the Starbucks is there. I as the knower of the field will have the desire to have a cup of coffee. That knowledge of the field by the knower is the propeller of action. As long as Im identified as the knower of the field constantly associating with the field that knowledge will create the impulse in me to act in this world. So thats clearly Bhagawan said you should understand that the knower of the field minus the field is just the knower.
Knowledge of the field minus the field is just the knowledge. So that knowledge is I exist in my deep sleep. I have no other knowledge but I still know that I exist. So when I wake up and somebody asks what kind of sleep? You say I had a very nice sleep. I said I dont know, I just had a good sleep.
There is no other experience but just I exist in the experience. Bhagavan said, know how these actions work. When the field comes in contact with the knower of the field when knowledge takes place that knowledge will be the propeller of your action. And then he says Karanam Karma Karta ITI Trivedha Karma Sangrah what will preserve the action? Three things to come together. Karanamdhi instrument of action.
I see a nice house in a good neighborhood. I really want to buy this house. But then I figure out: do I have the means to buy the house? If I dont have the means, all that good idea about that house and my desire to buy it remains just a dream. I will only put that into action if I have the means to perform that action -- that is Karanam.
When I have the Karana -- the means, the equipment to perform this action -- then we need the Karta, the doer. If there is no doer, I may have all the means and all the desires, but if I am not available to perform that action, then it wont come into existence. So these two have to come together. The Karanam and Karta have to come together for Karma to take place. We are analyzing what the impulse of action is, and how action comes into being, because at the end of this discussion were going to find out what control I have over my actions.
We are coming to the conclusion that the person that I really have control over is the Kartha. If I dont have that doership Bhav that notion that I am the doer then no action really takes place. So that I, which we call it the conditioned I Jivatma is thinking that he is the doer. Not only is thinking he is the doer, he is the only doer. When I perform any action and it is successful I feel that I did it and I did it all by myself. There was no help from anybody else.
This is where Bhagavan says you are going wrong. That you think you are the doer and you are the only doer. If I think that I have the control over my actions and I perform my actions then obviously I have a particular result in mind. Because I think Im performing it correctly. Im performing right field. The result must be X, Y or Z.
We forget that for any action I have to perform the field of action has to be appropriately configured to drive from my home to here. The whole field of action which is my road from my house to here has to be completely clear. All traffic lights have to work perfectly. All other drivers should drive in the proper lanes. Unless all that come in property configuration I wouldnt be able to come here in time. So when I consider that I did everything myself to come here in time, Im actually wrong.
There are so many people have to do so many things for me to be here on time.

These verses introduce the threefold classification of knowledge based on the gunas. Sattvic knowledge perceives the One immutable Reality in all diverse beings - seeing the undivided in the divided (verse 20). Rajasic knowledge sees beings as separate and unrelated, perceiving manifold distinct entities everywhere (verse 21). This distinction has immediate practical implications. When we have sattvic knowledge about our own body, our hand rushes to help our aching leg without negotiation - there is complete unity. But with rajasic knowledge about the world, we see others as fundamentally separate, requiring permission, contracts, and boundaries for any cooperation.
The key insight is that our type of knowledge determines our type of action. If I see the world as a collection of separate, competing entities (rajasic knowledge), my actions will naturally be self-protective and acquisitive. If I perceive the same consciousness animating all beings (sattvic knowledge), my actions become naturally harmonious and selfless - like the seamless coordination within my own body. The knower, the knowledge, and the knowable are the propellers of action. Transform the knowledge, and the actions transform automatically.
Examine your perception today: When you interact with family, colleagues, or strangers, what do you fundamentally see? Separate beings competing for limited resources? Or the same life force expressing through different forms? Choose one interaction today and consciously shift to sattvic perception - see the other person as another expression of the same consciousness that animates you. Notice how this shift in perception naturally changes the quality of your interaction, making it more easeful and compassionate.
